scope: SQLite child-process SIGKILL and durable Team claim recovery
scenario: Child process A opens the real SQLite journal and claims the task.
The test sends SIGKILL without invoking scheduler close or cleanup.
The original lease expires in the shared database.
Child process B opens the same journal and claims with a new owner/epoch.
The marker and journal row prove owner A epoch 1 then owner B epoch 2.
limitations: This slice proves durable claim recovery, not rollback of an already dispatched external side effect.
The child-process scenario is SQLite-only; PostgreSQL multi-instance process recovery remains to be run separately.
No default desktop Team or autonomous sub-agent activation is claimed.
